Tubulin brightening is reproduced across four independent single wells spanning 0.03-10 uM (tub_mean z +4.8 to +11.3, tub_std up throughout), tub_glcm_contrast reaches z=+30.4 at 10 uM, two independent phenotype reads report bundles/spiky elongated cells, and the atlas is 8/10 microtubule stabilizers (mean cosine 0.792 vs 0.68 for the single protein-degradation neighbour). reflection.text:
The stabilizer call was driven by a strong, reproduced tubulin signal: tub_mean z=+7.2 to +11.3 across 4 independent wells from 0.03 to 10 uM (e2, e3, e9), tub_glcm_contrast z=+30.4 at 10 uM (e2), two blinded phenotype reads reporting bundles/spiky cells (e4, e5), and atlas 8/10 microtubule stabilizers (e6). I over-weighted magnitude and reproducibility and treated tubulin brightening plus bundle texture as specific for taxane-like stabilization, raising Microtubule stabilizers to 0.92 while leaving Protein degradation at 0.01 despite it appearing as 1/10 atlas neighbour.

What I missed is that proteasome inhibitor I blocks turnover, so tubulin/MAPs accumulate and the MTOC remodels, which can look exactly like stabilization in a single tubulin intensity/texture channel. That literature link was present in this run (PMID 12928331; PMID 15564385) but I did not use it to challenge the hypothesis. The flat dose-response should have warned me: Spearman rho=+0.40 p=0.6 for tub_mean (e10) and rho=+0.40 p=0.6 for contrast (e12) with saturation already at the lowest dose, plus negative trend for frac_large_nucleus (e11), is atypical for a titratable stabilizer and more consistent with saturated accumulation/stress and cell-cycle arrest seen as nuc_dna_mean z=-6 to -7.6 with increased integrated DNA (e3, e8).

Acquisition choices locked in the error: I spent all 4 wells on single replicates spread across doses with no same-well replicate and exhausted budget (0/4 left), so I could not test variability, then accepted the reviewer's approval without a discriminating comparison. A ubiquitin or washout control instead of a fourth dose level would have separated blocked degradation from direct stabilization.

Approve. Tubulin brightening is reproduced across four independent single wells spanning 0.03-10 uM (tub_mean z +4.8 to +11.3, tub_std up throughout), tub_glcm_contrast reaches z=+30.4 at 10 uM, two independent phenotype reads report bundles/spiky elongated cells, and the atlas is 8/10 microtubule stabilizers (mean cosine 0.792 vs 0.68 for the single protein-degradation neighbour). Aurora kinase inhibition could explain the enlarged/integrated-DNA nuclei seen at mid dose, but it cannot explain the direction and magnitude of the tubulin increase, the bundle texture, or the atlas neighbourhood; microtubule destabilizers would predict the opposite tubulin direction. The weak, non-monotonic Spearman trends and the 1 uM contrast dip do not undermine the call because the tub_mean effect is already saturated at the lowest tested dose (z=+7.2 at 0.03 uM) and is measured in four different wells, so no result rests on a single well despite one replicate per dose. ## Unblinding

Compound: **proteasome inhibitor I** (PubChem CID [16760625](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/16760625))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Incorrect: agent said **Microtubule stabilizers**, BBBC021 annotates **Protein degradation**.

## Reflection

The stabilizer call was driven by a strong, reproduced tubulin signal: tub_mean z=+7.2 to +11.3 across 4 independent wells from 0.03 to 10 uM (e2, e3, e9), tub_glcm_contrast z=+30.4 at 10 uM (e2), two blinded phenotype reads reporting bundles/spiky cells (e4, e5), and atlas 8/10 microtubule stabilizers (e6). I over-weighted magnitude and reproducibility and treated tubulin brightening plus bundle texture as specific for taxane-like stabilization, raising Microtubule stabilizers to 0.92 while leaving Protein degradation at 0.01 despite it appearing as 1/10 atlas neighbour.

What I missed is that proteasome inhibitor I blocks turnover, so tubulin/MAPs accumulate and the MTOC remodels, which can look exactly like stabilization in a single tubulin intensity/texture channel. That literature link was present in this run (PMID 12928331; PMID 15564385) but I did not use it to challenge the hypothesis. The flat dose-response should have warned me: Spearman rho=+0.40 p=0.6 for tub_mean (e10) and rho=+0.40 p=0.6 for contrast (e12) with saturation already at the lowest dose, plus negative trend for frac_large_nucleus (e11), is atypical for a titratable stabilizer and more consistent with saturated accumulation/stress and cell-cycle arrest seen as nuc_dna_mean z=-6 to -7.6 with increased integrated DNA (e3, e8).

Acquisition choices locked in the error: I spent all 4 wells on single replicates spread across doses with no same-well replicate and exhausted budget (0/4 left), so I could not test variability, then accepted the reviewer's approval without a discriminating comparison. A ubiquitin or washout control instead of a fourth dose level would have separated blocked degradation from direct stabilization.

What was right:
- Measured a real, reproduced tubulin accumulation and texture change across 0.03-10 uM, not a single-well artifact
- Correctly noted reduced density and nuclear DNA shifts (low mean, high integrated) indicating cell-cycle/mitotic stress
- Correctly retained Aurora kinase inhibitors as minor alternative for enlarged nuclei and noted protein degradation as atlas minority (1/10)

What was wrong or missed:
- Misattributed tub_mean increase and high tub_glcm_contrast bundles specifically to microtubule stabilizers, ignoring proteasomal accumulation
- Dismissed flat/non-monotonic dose-response (rho +0.40, p=0.6) as saturation rather than evidence against direct stabilizer pharmacology
- Over-weighted 8/10 atlas vote and discounted the single protein-degradation neighbour that was the true MoA
- Exhausted acquisition budget on dose spread with n=1 per dose and no ubiquitin/washout counter-assay to test degradation vs stabilization

Proposed next experiment: Stain same dose range for polyubiquitin / proteasome activity reporter plus p62 and compare washout kinetics of tubulin bundles versus taxol: proteasome inhibitor should show ubiquitin puncta accumulation and persistent tubulin density dependent on blocked turnover, while true stabilizer shows EB1-comet suppression without ubiquitin buildup.
